Why should red wine not have equal rights?

Red wine isn’t a person or a sentient being, so “rights” don’t apply to it in the same way they apply to humans. People should have equal rights regardless of characteristics such as race, sex, or beliefs. Red wine can still be treated responsibly—for example, with regulations around labeling, safety, and fair trade—but it doesn’t need or possess personal rights.

Why should red wine not have equal rights?

Red wine isn’t a person or moral agent, so “rights” don’t literally apply to it. If you mean fair treatment among beverages, there’s no principled reason to deny red wine equal consideration—though laws may regulate its sale and consumption for public-health reasons.
